subject: Intermittent chunked latency (payload emit oscillation) — initial notice & short-term steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@clearbridgelabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent chunked latency (payload emit oscillation) — initial notice & short-term steps

Samantha —

Quick heads-up from our side: we detected intermittent high-latency spikes affecting streaming responses to your websocket-based conversational endpoint starting ~07:58 PDT this morning. The symptom looks like brief "chunked" frames where tokens are buffered on the server for ~300-800ms before being emitted in bursts (you may see short periods where the UI appears to stall then catch up).

Impact: noticeable pauses for end-users on longer responses (especially >250 tokens). Error rates have stayed low; requests complete, but token emission pacing is irregular which degrades perceived responsiveness.

What we're doing now:
- Ingesting trace-level logs and KV cache telemetry (already collected)
- Rolling limited routing changes to reduce load on one edge-pop we suspect is oscillating
- Enabling a temporary conservative batching profile for your account to avoid large multi-request batches that amplify the delay

Short-term steps you can apply (no code change required, two quick config toggles):
1) On your client, enable smaller chunk reads (reduce socket frame buffer to 512–1024 bytes) — this will let partial tokens be surfaced earlier.
2) Increase client-side streaming read timeout to 5s and add a lightweight retry at 1.5s for stalled frames; this avoids spurious disconnects during transient stalls.

I've attached a small diagnostic payload sample and logs. Our SREs are working on root-cause; I'll follow up with an update within 2 hours or sooner if anything changes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your UX. We'll own fixing and share a concrete post-incident plan.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Park <samantha@clearbridgelabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent chunked latency (payload emit oscillation) — initial notice & short-term steps

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick update. We're seeing the pauses in the customer-facing chat widget — the support queue spike started shortly after 08:00. Our product team is anxious about a scheduled demo at 10:30 PT.

We applied the client buffer/read timeout suggestion (512 bytes, 5s timeout) and it helped reduce visible stalls in a quick smoke test. Can you confirm whether the routing change is account-scoped or global? Also: ETA on when you expect a rollback to normal pacing?

— Sam
Lead Platform Engineer, ClearBridge Labs

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent chunked latency — immediate ops/CX actions

Folks — forwarding Sam's note. TL;DR: customer-facing stalls due to token emission oscillation on edge-pop eu-west-2a (we're seeing uneven shard load + temporary IO backlog). Action items: 
- Laura: confirm whether account-specific routing already pinned CB to a single shard; if so, force-redistribute to a different healthy shard and watch token emit cadence (counterfactual test).
- Monica: collect KV-cache hit stats and socket backlog metrics for the timeframe 07:45–08:20; dump sample frames for inspection and attach to the ticket.
- Logan: prepare a canned opt-in client config (two lines) we can give Sam for the demo — include the buffer/read-timeout and disabled aggressive prefetch.

We should avoid a full-scale rollback unless the redis patch is safe; prefer targeted routing moves + conservative batching until root cause is confirmed.

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent chunked latency (payload emit oscillation) — mitigation applied & client config

Sam —

Thanks for confirming the symptom and for applying the client-side adjustments. Quick status: we've moved ClearBridge's routing off the affected edge shard and applied a more conservative batching profile for your account at 09:48 PT. Early telemetry looks improved (median token emit gap dropped from ~420ms to ~90ms in sampled requests).

Attached is the two-line snippet Logan prepared (paste into your streaming client config):
- streaming.read_buffer_bytes = 1024
- streaming.prefetch = false

We've prioritized your demo window and will keep the routing and conservative batching for the next 24 hours while we validate stability. We're also continuing post-incident analysis and will send a full timeline + root cause when ready.

If you want, I can join the demo at 10:30 to keep an eye on the session.

— Karthik

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@clearbridgelabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: payload emission oscillation (03 Mar 2027) — root cause & mitigations

Sam —

Appreciate your patience while we completed the postmortem. Summary and actions below; attaching the postmortem PDF for internal/regulator review.

What happened (summary):
- Time window: 2027-03-03 07:58–10:10 PT.
- Symptom: short-duration token emission buffering (300–900ms) observed on a subset of streaming requests to your account; requests completed but token pacing created perceived stalls.
- Root cause: a combination of (1) an autoscaler bug that temporarily over-packed streams onto a single edge shard under a brief load pattern, and (2) a regression in our continuous batching heuristic that allowed a rare batch compaction path to hold frames slightly longer than intended when combined with a bursty L7 proxy retransmit pattern.

Immediate corrective actions we took:
- Rebalanced ClearBridge traffic away from the impacted shard and applied a conservative batching profile (done 09:48 PT on 03 Mar).
- Rolled back the batching heuristic patch and deployed a safe fallback to the previous batching kernel (03 Mar 11:05 PT).
- Deployed a fix to the autoscaler placement heuristics to avoid extreme packing in the face of short-lived bursts (deployed 05 Mar 02:20 PT).

Planned improvements (next 90 days):
- Add a safety limit on per-shard stream packing and a fallback path to stream-by-token emission when buffers exceed 200ms.
- Improve observability: per-tenant token-emit histograms surfaced in Console + alert rule for median emit gaps >200ms sustained for 5 minutes.
- Client guidance: we'll publish a best-practice snippet for websocket read-buffer sizing and prove a zero-config client-side fallback for the most common SDKs.

Customer impact & remediation:
- We estimate 0.6% of streaming requests for ClearBridge during the window exhibited noticeable stalls.
- As a goodwill gesture, we've applied a service credit equivalent to one week's streaming overage for your account (ref DEAL-4721). I'll have billing send the formal credit note.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-20270308.pdf (timeline, logs excerpt), diagnostic_logs_20270303.zip.

If you'd like a short walkthrough of the postmortem with the engineering team, we can schedule a 30-minute session — I can join early next week.

Thanks again for flagging this and for working with us on the quick mitigations.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
